'''Elvira Maria Correia Fortunato''' {{post-nominals|post-noms=[[Order of Prince Henry|GOIH]]}} (born 22 July 1964) is a Portuguese scientist and minister of science and technology. She is a professor in the Department of Materials Science at the [[NOVA School of Science and Technology]] and vice-rector of the [[NOVA University Lisbon]]. Fortunato is an innovator in the field of paper [[electronics]], including [[transistor]]s, memories, [[sensor]]s, batteries, [[Display device|displays]], antennas, and [[solar cell]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Short CV Elvira Fortunato|url=https://ec.europa.eu/research/sam/pdf/cv/cv_e-fortunato_2015.pdf|last=|first=|date=|website=European Commission|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.intechopen.com/books/nanostructured-solar-cells|title=Nanostructured Solar Cells|date=2017-02-22|publisher=InTech|isbn=978-953-51-2935-6|editor-last=Das|editor-first=Narottam|language=en|doi=10.5772/62516}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Elvira MC Fortunato's Publons profile|url=https://publons.com/researcher/2789270/elvira-mc-fortunato/|website=publons.com|language=en|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref>

In 2022, Fortunato was appointed [[Ministry of Science, Technology and Higher Education|Minister of Science, Technology and Higher Education]] in the [[XXIII Constitutional Government of Portugal]] as an [[Independent politician|independent]], succeeding [[Manuel Heitor]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jn.pt/nacional/a-cientista-que-vai-tomar-conta-da-ciencia-e-do-superior-14708200.html |title=Elvira Fortunato: a cientista que vai tomar conta da Ciência e do Superior |last=Inácio |first=Alexandra |date=23 March 2022 |website= |publisher=[[Jornal de Notícias]] |access-date=24 March 2022 |quote=}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Fortunato was born in [[Almada]], and received her degree in [[Materials science|Materials Science]] and [[Physics]] in 1987 from the [[NOVA School of Science and Technology]] and continued her graduate studies at the same university. In 1991, Fortunato received her master's degree in Semiconductor Materials and in 1995, her Ph.D. in [[Microelectronics]] and [[Optoelectronics]]. In 2005, she obtained her habilitation in the same field.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Elvira Fortunato {{!}} CENIMAT|url=https://www.cenimat.fct.unl.pt/pessoas/people/elvira-fortunato|website=www.cenimat.fct.unl.pt|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref>

== Career ==
Fortunato joined the faculty at the [[NOVA School of Science and Technology]] in 1995 and became director of the Institute of Nanostructures, Nanomodeling, and Nanofabrication in 1998. She led a research team that achieved acclaim for inventing the paper transistor in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 May 2016|title=Microchips made of paper: Elvira Fortunato and Rodrigo Martins named European Inventor Award 2016 finalists|url=https://www.advancedsciencenews.com/microchips-made-of-paper/|access-date=21 February 2021|website=Advanced Science News}}</ref>

Fortunato is an elected member of Academy of Engineering, European Academy of Sciences, [[Lisbon Academy of Sciences]], and [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Fortunato_Elvira |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200521094624/https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Fortunato_Elvira |title=Elvira Fortunato |publisher=Academia Europaea |date= |archive-date=21 May 2020}}</ref> She is Associate Editor of ''Rapid Research Letters Physica Status Solidi'', Co-Editor of ''[[Europhysics Letters]]'', and an Editorial Advisory Board Member of ''[[ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces]]''.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Elvira Fortunato (0000-0002-4202-7047)|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4202-7047|last=ORCID|website=orcid.org|language=en|access-date=2020-05-10}}</ref>

She has been the vice-rector of [[NOVA University Lisbon]] since 2017 and is in charge of coordinating the university's research.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-09-26 |title=Elvira Fortunato |url=https://www.unl.pt/pessoas/elvira-fortunato |access-date=2022-04-08 |website=Universidade NOVA de Lisboa |language=pt-pt}}</ref>

In 2022, she was part of a group of 27 inspiring women from Europe, elected by the current French Presidency of the European Union.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2022-03-24 |title=Elvira Fortunato appointed as Minister of Science, Technology and Higher Education |url=https://www.fct.unl.pt/en/news/2022/03/elvira-fortunato-appointed-minister-science-technology-and-higher-education |access-date=2022-03-27 |website=fct.unl.pt}}</ref>

In March 2022, she joined the Government of the Portuguese Republic as Minister of Science, Technology, and Higher Education.<ref name=":3" />

== Research ==
Fortunato's research focuses on exploring new electronic active materials that are [[environmentally friendly]] and compatible with [[flexible electronics]]. This led to the invention of the first paper transistor in 2008, which used paper, a low-cost and flexible [[biopolymer]], as the insulator layer (gate dielectric) of a thin-film transistor, replacing the commonly used silicon.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Full Page Reload|url=https://spectrum.ieee.org/paper-transistor|website=IEEE Spectrum: Technology, Engineering, and Science News|language=en|access-date=2020-05-20}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Martins|first1=Rodrigo|last2=Barquinha|first2=Pedro|last3=Pereira|first3=Luís|last4=Correia|first4=Nuno|last5=Gonçalves|first5=Gonçalo|last6=Ferreira|first6=Isabel|last7=Fortunato|first7=Elvira|date=2008-11-17|title=Write-erase and read paper memory transistor|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/full/10.1063/1.3030873|journal=Applied Physics Letters|volume=93|issue=20|pages=203501|doi=10.1063/1.3030873|bibcode=2008ApPhL..93t3501M|issn=0003-6951|hdl=10362/3962|hdl-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She pioneered European research on transparent electronics, namely [[thin-film transistor]]s based on oxide [[semiconductor]]s, demonstrating that [[oxide]] materials can be used as true semiconductors.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research {{!}} CENIMAT|url=https://www.cenimat.fct.unl.pt/rd-id-teams/materials-electronics-optoelectronics-and-nanotechnologies/research|website=www.cenimat.fct.unl.pt|access-date=2020-05-10|archive-date=June 5, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200605135634/https://www.cenimat.fct.unl.pt/rd-id-teams/materials-electronics-optoelectronics-and-nanotechnologies/research|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Research activities {{!}} Elvira Fortunato|url=https://docentes.fct.unl.pt/emf/pages/research-activities|website=docentes.fct.unl.pt|language=en|access-date=2020-05-11}}</ref>

Fortunato's paper electronics technology has applications that include [[biosensor]]s, radiofrequency identification ([[Radio-frequency identification|RFID]]) tags in shipping, and product inventory management <ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Microchips made of paper: Elvira Fortunato and Rodrigo Martins named European Inventor Award 2016 finalists|url=https://www.advancedsciencenews.com/microchips-made-of-paper/|date=2016-05-13|website=Advanced Science News|language=en-US|access-date=2020-05-11}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==

Fortunato has received national and international awards for her work.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Recent Awards {{!}} Elvira Fortunato|url=https://docentes.fct.unl.pt/emf/pages/recent-awards|website=docentes.fct.unl.pt|language=en|access-date=2020-05-11}}</ref> In 2005, she received the prize for Scientific Excellence from the [[Fundação para a Ciência e Tecnologia|Portuguese Foundation for Science and Technology]]. In 2009, she was cited by the [[Portuguese Parliament]] for her research. In 2010, she was awarded membership in the [[Order of Prince Henry]] by then-Portuguese President [[Aníbal Cavaco Silva]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ordens Nacionais - Pagina Oficial das Ordens Honorificas Portuguesas |url=http://www.ordens.presidencia.pt/?idc=111&idi=5779 |website=Orden Honorificas Portuguesas |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200901173949/http://www.ordens.presidencia.pt/?idc=111&idi=5779|access-date=1 September 2020|archive-date = September 1, 2020}}</ref> In 2015, she was President of [[Portugal Day]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Elvira Fortunato presides 10th June Celebrations |url=https://www.fct.unl.pt/en/news/2015/06/professor-elvira-fortunato-presides-10th-june-celebrations |website=Universidade Nova de Lisboa |publisher=fct.unl.pt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200901174502/https://www.fct.unl.pt/en/news/2015/06/professor-elvira-fortunato-presides-10th-june-celebrations |access-date=1 September 2020|archive-date=September 1, 2020 }}</ref> In 2016, she was awarded the Blaise Pascal Medal in materials science by the European Academy of Sciences<ref>{{cite web |title=EURASC Awardees |url=https://www.eurasc.org/eurasc-awardees/blaise-pascal-medals |website=European Academy of Sciences |publisher=www.eurasc.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807221955/https://www.eurasc.org/eurasc-awardees/blaise-pascal-medals |access-date=1 September 2020|archive-date=August 7, 2020 }}</ref> and in 2017, the Czochralski award in recognition of her research work in the area of Advanced Materials Science. In 2018, she received a [[European Research Council]] grant worth €3.5 million, the largest grant ever awarded to a Portuguese researcher at the time of the award.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Elvira Fortunato, Vice-Rector of NOVA, Receives Maximum Amount ERC Advanced Grant for the First Time Awarded to Portugal |url=https://www.unl.pt/en/news/general/professor-elvira-fortunato-vice-rector-nova-receives-maximum-amount-erc-advanced-grant |website=Universidade Nova de Lisboa |date=April 4, 2018 |publisher=www.unl.pt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180424015358/https://www.unl.pt/en/news/general/professor-elvira-fortunato-vice-rector-nova-receives-maximum-amount-erc-advanced-grant |access-date=1 September 2020|archive-date=April 24, 2018 }}</ref> She was the recipient of the 2020 [[Pessoa Prize]], recognized as the most important award of the Portuguese culture.
